KPro/Project guide

A PROJECT-LEVEL WALKTHROUGH

Build an order service.
Not another hello world.

Start with business rules, expose them through HTTP and a message transport, then make startup, shutdown, observability and validation explicit.

Start with the domain↓ Read the golden path↗

A design blueprint, not a production capacity claim.
01

DOMAIN FIRST

Organize around the business,
not the transport.

HTTP and TCP are delivery mechanisms. The order service owns rules; adapters translate requests and events at the edge.

cmd/orders/main.goPROJECT ROLE

Own process assembly

Create dependencies, register middleware, mount transports, wait for readiness, and translate process signals into cancellation.

RuleKeep business decisions out of main.
HTTP Handlerdecode + map
→
Order Servicebusiness rules
→
Order Storeapplication port
02

ONE SERVICE, MULTIPLE EDGES

Share business logic.
Keep protocol semantics.

HTTP handlers keep request/response semantics. Message handlers keep Message / Context and per-session ordering. Both call the same application service.

Why this boundary?

03

PROCESS OWNERSHIP

Make the happy path
and the shutdown path visible.

A service is not ready when main returns from construction. Publish readiness only after every readiness-aware runner has bound successfully.

  1. 01
    Open dependenciesValidate config and connect required resources before traffic.
  2. 02
    Assemble onceRegister middleware, routes, transports and managed resources.
  3. 03
    Start + WaitReadyDistinguish listener readiness from startup failure.
  4. 04
    Cancel + drainStop admission, drain accepted work, then close resources.
!

A transport write receipt confirms the write boundary—not peer processing, durable delivery, or business acknowledgement.

04

TEST FROM THE INSIDE OUT

Turn assumptions
into evidence.

Repository tests prove framework behavior. Your application still owns its latency, data correctness, failure recovery and safe capacity.

01

Domain tests

Exercise order rules with fake ports and no listener.

fast · deterministic

protocol boundary

Integration tests
